content: Poonam had a fever and had to stay home. While resting on her cot under a tree, she noticed a whole world above her! Pigeons, squirrels, crows, and even tiny ants were busy going about their day. Have you ever wondered how many different types of animals live right outside your window?
Imagine you are sitting under that same tree. You see a bird, a squirrel, and an ant. How do they move from one branch to another? Do they all move the same way? What about the animals in a pond?

content.title: Ways Animals Move
content.description: Observe how different animals use their bodies to move around their surroundings.

content: Animals can be grouped by how they move and where they live! Some walk on land, some fly in the air using wings, some crawl, and some swim in water. The place where an animal naturally lives is called its habitat.

definition: The natural home or environment of an animal, plant, or other organism.
Moving forward on the hands and knees or by dragging the body close to the ground, like a snake or a lizard.

question: Poonam went to the pond to wash her face. Which of these animals would she most likely see swimming there?
Which of these animals moves by crawling or slithering?

content: Think about your favorite animal. Does it walk, fly, swim, or crawl? Where does it spend most of its day? If you were that animal, how would you move around?

Just like humans have different houses and vehicles, animals have their own special homes and ways to travel. Understanding this helps us realize how beautifully diverse nature is and why we must protect different habitats like forests and ponds!
Look outside your window or visit a park. Make a list of 5 animals you see. Group them by how they move: Walking, Flying, or Crawling. Try mimicking their sounds and movements!
Encourage students to act out the movements and sounds of the animals they discuss. It makes the classification process intuitive and memorable.
Students often think all birds can fly, or that insects are not animals. Remind them that ostriches are birds that walk, and insects are a type of animal too!
